text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 9.1px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start

g.text: How it works: hold the switch UP -> pole A feeds +12 V into the M+ line, pole B grounds the M- line -> seats rise. At the top the UP limit opens; D1 blocks the UP current
so the motors stop, but D1 still conducts the opposite (DOWN) current, so you can always drive back down. The DOWN limit + D2 work the same way at the bottom. Let go -> the switch
springs to OFF and both motor leads float -> seats stop instantly. The key switch and E-stop kill everything. Nothing here is controlled by software; the game can only READ the sense input.
Fuse: ~1.25 x the sum of both actuators' rated running current and below the wire's rating (e.g. 2 x 3 A -> 7.5 A blade fuse, 16 AWG). If the key switch is rated for less
than that current, let it switch the coil of a 12 V 30 A automotive relay instead. Mount the hold-to-run switch where only dad's seat can reach it and the kids' seats are in view.
Prefer actuators with BUILT-IN limit switches; these external limits then set the real travel inside that range. If the two actuators are not tied to one rigid frame, give each
actuator its own UP/DOWN limit pair + diodes. Diodes must carry the full motor current. Add pinch-point guards; seat up only after harnesses are fastened.
